## The Regression Context

This was a regression in Django 2.1+ where the permission logic for auto-created through models became too permissive, allowing view-only users to modify inline data when they should only be able to view it.

Answer: The key discovery was that permission methods for auto-created ManyToMany through models were incorrectly allowing any user with view permission to add, change, or delete inline items. The fix required checking for the specific matching permission (add/change/delete) on the related model, rather than just checking for view permission.

tep 48 of the materials:

> The fix should:
> 1. For `has_add_permission()`: Check if user has add permission on the related model
> 2. For `has_change_permission()`: Check if user has change permission on the related model
> 3. For `has_delete_permission()`: Check if user has delete permission on the related model

These three methods in the `InlineModelAdmin` class (located around lines 2114-2139 in options.py) were incorrectly returning `self.has_view_permission(request, obj)` for auto-created models, which allowed view-only users to add, change, and delete items in inline forms.
